step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture represents Mobileye's Dynamic RAM mobility intelligence platform. It processes sensor and visual inspection data collected from vehicles worldwide. The architecture has four major stages: Ingestion (Vehicles to REST API to Raw S3), Processing (Raw S3 triggers SQS, consumed by auto-scaling Process EKS workers which orchestrate algorithms via Step Functions and output data to Store S3, Elasticsearch, and CockroachDB), Storage, and Consumption (API Gateway for enterprise city planners/customers, and a Consume EKS backend serving a Web App to end users). All services use valid vocabulary entries, with CockroachDB mapped to ThirdParty and Elasticsearch mapped to OpenSearch.

graph.name: Mobileye Dynamic RAM Mobility Intelligence Architecture
graph.notes: Dynamic RAM processes 10M daily observations from vehicles using an auto-scaling EKS cluster (100 to 800 workers), Step Functions state machines, and dynamic storage across S3, Elasticsearch, and CockroachDB.

nodes.name: Vehicles
nodes.notes: Vehicles collecting anonymized sensor and visual inspection data on roads worldwide.

nodes.name: REST API
nodes.notes: Ingestion REST API located in a separate AWS account to ingest raw data from vehicles.

nodes.name: Raw S3 Bucket
nodes.notes: Stores raw incoming vehicle observation data.

nodes.name: SQS
nodes.notes: Buffer queue that triggers and distributes processing workload to EKS workers.

nodes.name: Process EKS Workers
nodes.notes: Scales automatically from 100 to 800 workers based on SQS queue size to process 10M daily observations.

nodes.name: Step Functions
nodes.notes: Orchestrates complex algorithm execution flows (e.g., detecting construction zones, clustering, aggregation).

nodes.name: Store S3 Bucket
nodes.notes: Stores preprocessed, formatted, and algorithm-calculated output data.

nodes.name: Elasticsearch
nodes.notes: Document-based self-indexing search store for quick querying of mobility intelligence.

nodes.name: CockroachDB
nodes.notes: Distributed relational database hosted on EKS to support high-frequency updates to tables.

nodes.name: Consume API Gateway
nodes.notes: Exposes REST API endpoints for enterprise customers and city planners.

nodes.name: Consume EKS Cluster
nodes.notes: Serves secured REST API backend and powers web application data access.

nodes.name: Web App
nodes.notes: Web application interface for visualizing mobility intelligence and live traffic events.

nodes.name: Enterprise Customers
nodes.notes: City planners and road operators consuming traffic, pedestrian, and construction zone insights.

nodes.name: End Users
nodes.notes: End consumers accessing mobility services and real-time road insights.

edges.notes: Vehicles send collected sensor data to the ingestion REST API.
REST API writes incoming raw data to Raw S3 bucket.
Raw S3 bucket triggers/enqueues work items into SQS.
Process EKS workers pull messages from SQS and scale based on queue depth.
EKS workers trigger Step Functions for parallel algorithm flows.
EKS workers directly format and store preprocessed data into Store S3.
EKS workers store calculated observations and document indices in Elasticsearch.
EKS workers write high-frequency updates into CockroachDB.
Step Functions output algorithmic processing results into Store S3.
Store S3 data is exposed via API Gateway to enterprise users.
Elasticsearch provides indexed search data to Consume EKS Cluster.
CockroachDB provides relational state data to Consume EKS Cluster.
API Gateway provides mobility API access to enterprise customers.
Consume EKS Cluster serves backend services for the Web App.
Web App delivers interactive mobility dashboards to end users.
